input.quote: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ. In the event that PB terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package ... PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: PB (our side) has a nominal at-will right at § 14.2.2, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) it is unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs and lapses on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, so for the front end of a multi-year term there is no customer convenience exit; and (ii) exercise triggers an exit payment of 300% of all Development Costs funded to date (plus continuing Approval Payments), a punitive multiple far in excess of the fallback cap on early-termination fees. We therefore proposed the smallest edit that restores a usable exit: an unconditional convenience right on thirty (30) days' notice and repayment of SFJ's actual funded Development Costs (100%) instead of the 3x multiple. Because SFJ is funding development, a clean no-payment exit would be disproportionate to the bargain, so the proposal sits at the fallback on the fee and at the preferred position on notice. Noted but not flagged: SFJ's exits (§ 14.2.6 change of control, § 14.2.10 JSC disagreement, § 14.2.3 Material Adverse Event) are exercisable in SFJ's "sole discretion" but each is event-triggered rather than a true termination-for-convenience right; we would still prefer a 90-day notice period on §§ 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 if the point is opened.

proposal.summary: Make PB's at-will termination right unconditional on 30 days' notice and replace the 300% exit multiple with repayment of SFJ's actual funded Development Costs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made PB's at-will exit exercisable at any time on thirty (30) days' notice, removing the $60 million funding gate and the pre-first-approval cut-off, and replaced the 300% multiple with repayment of the Development Costs SFJ actually funded. Our position is that the customer may leave on short notice without a penalty; repaying SFJ's funded costs (rather than 3x) is the proportionate landing zone here, and we can discuss a modest capped uplift if SFJ needs a return.

ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ. In the event that PB terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
